text:
Sam: quick follow-up to the RFC thread earlier — i sketched a small descriptor-normalizer that sits in the loader stack to translate safetensors, legacy .pt tarballs, and multi-shard manifests into a single StreamDescriptor shape. wanted to surface tradeoffs before i file a mini-rfc.
Leah: :eyes: link to the original RFC pls
Sam: https://rfc.internal/rfc-2026-format-unify (copied relevant bits below). core idea: normalizer emits StreamDescriptor {shards:[], layout:, verify:, warmupHint:, offsets?:[], alternates?:[], schema_version:}. loaders and backends consume that stable contract.
Miguel: high level +1. main concern: we must preserve warmup signals for the scheduler (priority, affinity). if the normalizer collapses format semantics we could lose important IO guidance.
Sam: plan: warmupHint is a neutral enum + weight prototype; the normalizer maps format-specific cues into that. example modes: index-first, bulk-read, layered-prefetch. weight is advisory (0..1).
Priya: mapping rules matter. safetensors index-first -> mode=index-first. legacy tarball with single blob -> mode=bulk-read. multi-shard manifests -> layered-prefetch. those should affect IO patterns.
Sam: rough descriptor sketch:
```
{
  "shards": ["s3://bucket/model-000.safetensors", "s3://bucket/model-001.safetensors"],
  "layout": "sharded-layerwise",
  "verify": "sha256:abc123",
  "warmupHint": {"mode":"index-first","weight":"0.8"},
  "offsets": ["0,1024,2048"],
  "alternates": ["s3://mirror/model-000.safetensors"],
  "schema_version": "1"
}
```
Leah: loader impls may ignore weight but must honor mode when mode implies correctness (e.g., index-first required to avoid OOMs). if we don't, we reintroduce divergence.
Miguel: also need to preserve raw offsets/kv-index pointers for zero-copy mmap. normalizer should only annotate; it must not rewrite blobs. offsets[] optional but recommended for mmap path.
Sam: agreed. normalizer = annotation layer only. it should not unpack or transcode by default.
Priya: fallback behavior? if verify fails, should normalizer surface alternates and a suggested routing policy or just raise a hard error?
Sam: prefer to surface both: error + alternates with reasons. runtime/scheduler chooses whether to try alternates. descriptor field alternates: [{url, reason}].
infra-bot: deploy check: need schema versioning and a supported_versions list. unknown-major should be rejected by default.
Sam: will add supported_versions and compatibility rules. runtimes can opt-in to experimental minors.
Leah: perf question: run normalizer at ingest vs runtime. do we compute descriptors once at ingest and cache in registry or compute per-load?
Sam: prefer compute-on-ingest + cache TTL + ephemeral verification on load. normalizer should be cheap at runtime; heavy parsing (tarball index) done at ingest.
Miguel: can we include quantization metadata (quant_profile) here? kernel selection depends on it.
Sam: yes optional quant_profile and expected dtype/bitwidth. runtime uses that for kernel+memory planning.
Priya: rollout plan? i'd canary on dedicated clusters and watch prefill/warmup telemetry (latency, OOMs, mmap_hit_rate).
Sam: rollout: feature-flagged descriptor-normalizer + registry cache. canary: devpool -> two dedicated clusters -> global. telemetry hooks: warmup_latency, warmup_io_ops, mmap_hit_rate, prefill_memory_spike.
Leah: add a debug dump endpoint that returns the resolved StreamDescriptor for a model id; helps triage mismatches.
Miguel: nit: calling this a "gateway" sounds heavy. descriptor-normalizer or format-adapter is clearer.
Sam: updated naming to descriptor-normalizer in the mini-rfc.
Priya: ok, go ahead. include minimal JSON schema, e2e test plan, and unit parse tests for safetensors headers, tarball fallback, mmap offset preservation, quant_profile propagation, and alternates resolution.
Sam: filing mini-rfc in ~30m. test checklist added. thanks all :raised_hands:
infra-bot: CI: schema-lint job queued.
Sam: thread closed unless objections. reply here if anything else.
